record.title: The triage is the product: running AI agents against Ethereum's protocol code | Ethereum Foundation Blog
record.text:
Notes from the Ethereum Foundation's Protocol Security team on running coordinated AI agents against real protocol code, including how we organize the work, what holds up under scrutiny, and what client teams and security researchers can take from it. This post stands on its own; later posts will go deeper on individual clients.
What we've been running, and what surprised us
On the Ethereum Foundation's Protocol Security team, we've been running coordinated AI agents against the kinds of systems the network depends on, like systems software, cryptographic code, and contracts that have to be right. The agents found real bugs. One is now public: a remotely-triggerable panic in libp2p's gossipsub, a core part of the peer-to-peer layer Ethereum consensus clients run on, fixed and disclosed as CVE-2026-34219 with credit to the team.
Agents finding bugs wasn't the surprise. The surprise was how little of the work went into finding them, and how much went into telling the real bugs from the ones that just looked real.
This post is for client teams and security researchers who want to do the same thing. It covers how we organize the agents, the bar a candidate has to clear before it counts as a finding, and the habits that keep the results trustworthy.

[…]
A person makes the final call: agents suggest. They don't decide what's real, what's a duplicate of a known issue, or what gets disclosed and when.

record.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board's annual bank stress test confirms that large banks are well positioned to weather a severe recession and able to continue to lend to households and businesses
record.text:
June 24, 2026
Federal Reserve Board's annual bank stress test confirms that large banks are well positioned to weather a severe recession and able to continue to lend to households and businesses
For release at 4:00 p.m. EDT
Share
The results of the Federal Reserve Board's annual bank stress test confirmed that large banks are well positioned to weather a severe recession and able to continue to lend to households and businesses. Despite absorbing more than $708 billion in total losses under this year's hypothetical scenario, capital declined only 1.6 percentage points in aggregate, staying above minimum capital requirements.
"Today's results underscore the strength of the banking system," Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman said. "As we work to increase the transparency and accountability of the stress test, public feedback will help us continue to improve and instill greater confidence in the stress test and its results."
As the Board previously announced, today's results will not impact large bank capital requirements, which have been published today. The current capital requirements will stay in place until 2027, when the stress test will be run with loss-estimating models that take public feedback into consideration.
All 32 banks tested remained above their minimum common equity tier 1 capital requirements during this year's hypothetical recession scenario, which was similar in severity to the prior test. The hypothetical scenario this year included a severe global recession with a 39 percent decline in commercial real estate prices and a 30 percent decline in house prices. The unemployment rate also increased to a peak of 10 percent, and economic output declined commensurately.
Three main factors influenced the results of this year's test, with two leading to a larger decline in the aggregate capital ratio than last year, and one more than offsetting this decline:
Projected capital decreased from higher loan losses due to increased loan balances and the increased severity of certain scenario variables;
Projected capital decreased from lower projected unrealized gains in bank securities due to smaller hypothetical declines in interest rates during the scenario; and
Projected capital increased from higher interest income due to recent bank financial performance and smaller hypothetical declines of interest rates during the scenario.
The total projected losses include roughly $200 billion in credit card losses, $160 billion in losses from commercial and industrial loans, and $75 billion in losses from commercial real estate.
For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955.

2026 Large Bank Capital Requirements (PDF)
Note: On July 2, 2026, the following sentence was updated to remove the word loan, “Despite absorbing more than $708 billion in total loan losses under this year's hypothetical scenario, capital declined only 1.6 percentage points in aggregate, staying above minimum capital requirements.”

record.title: Solana Alpenglow Goes Live in 'Most Ambitious' Upgrade Since Ethereum's Merge - Decrypt
record.text:
In brief
Solana's new Alpenglow consensus protocol has gone live on mainnet-beta, replacing TowerBFT at slot 459,653,000, core developer Anza said.
Transactions now become irreversible in about 150 milliseconds, down from 12.8 seconds, which Anza says matters for exchanges, banks and merchants.
Further upgrades, including a post-quantum version called Quantumglow, are planned but have no committed dates.
Solana's largest consensus upgrade since the network launched in 2020 went live on Wednesday, cutting the time it takes for a transaction to become irreversible from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds, core engineering team Anza said.
Validators retired TowerBFT, the consensus protocol Solana had used since March 2020, at slot 459,653,000 at around 14:00 UTC. They switched systems on the running network while carrying its existing ledger forward, with independent operators coordinating a shared handoff point.
The change is to finality, the point at which a transaction can no longer be reversed and the moment an exchange, bank or merchant waits for before treating an asset as moved. Under TowerBFT, Solana gave a conditional confirmation within seconds but took about 12.8 seconds to reach full finality. Alpenglow condenses those two steps into one.

[…]
More upgrades are planned. Rotor will change how block data spreads across the network, and geographically aware leader rotation aims to cut delays as block production passes between validators. Quantumglow, a research design, would swap Alpenglow's elliptic-curve cryptography for hash-based signatures to make it secure against quantum computers while keeping the same finality speed. None has a committed date.Myriad: Where does Solana go next? Click to make your prediction.

record.title: Bitcoin Core Rewrites Its Security Policy for a World Where AI Finds Bugs in One Prompt - Decrypt
record.text:
In brief
Bitcoin Core updated its security policy to handle vulnerabilities that are “easily discoverable,” citing a spike in reports of bugs that LLMs have “drastically reduced the bar” to find.
For such flaws, the project will now backport a fix to all maintained releases and ship a new version as fast as possible—with an advisory—rather than keeping it under a long embargo, since a quiet patch “would achieve little” when an AI scan can find it anyway.
The shift reflects how AI has reshaped Bitcoin security, from the “Bitcoin Red Team” to AI-surfaced Lightning and wallet bugs.
Bitcoin Core developers have changed how the software handles certain security flaws, acknowledging that AI has made some vulnerabilities so easy to find that keeping them secret no longer makes sense.
The project merged the policy update Thursday, after Chaincode Labs developer Antoine Poinsot opened it earlier this month citing a spike in reports of bugs that can be “easily (re-)discovered.”Myriad: Which company will have the best AI model? Click to make your prediction.
The reason, Poinsot wrote, is that large language models have “drastically reduced the bar” to find certain classes of issues or to spot a quietly shipped fix in the code.

record.text:
Glad to see Lido exploring lending. I think lending is one of the most important primitives for making onchain capital markets work, and there’s a strong case for building more around stETH.
That said, I’m not convinced a modified Morpho Blue fork is the right approach, especially for a product positioning itself as security-first.
One of Morpho Blue’s strengths is its simple, immutable and extensively reviewed core. Once you start modifying it even by a few lines, you’re introducing new security assumptions. That doesn’t necessarily make it unsafe, but the original audits, formal verification and track record don’t automatically carry over. For lenders, it’s another set of contracts they need to evaluate and trust.

record.title: Unveiling Lido Lend: Security-First Lending — post 11
record.text:
Lido Lend Feature Highlight #1: Fallback Exits
Today we are excited to present the first of Lido Lend’s unique user features, dubbed Fallback Exits, a novel lending mechanism built to provide lenders with a secure and predictable liquidity exit path in times of turbulence.
Understanding Fallback Exits
In traditional lending markets, when loan asset liquidity dries up, lenders who want to withdraw are put in a position where they must wait for liquidity to return. This waiting can take days, or even weeks, before lenders regain access to a liquid position.
Fallback Exits are designed to address this need, by giving lenders an always available withdrawal path: when loan asset liquidity is insufficient, lenders can ‘Fallback Exit’ by using borrower collateral to supplement the withdrawal request.
Since Lido Lend consists of isolated markets and highly correlated assets (e.g. wETH <> wstETH, or USD <> Treasury RWAs), the option of exiting into borrower collateral (wholly or in part) provides a path to liquidity, even in extreme market turbulence.
Taking the ETH <> wstETH market as an example:
Assuming ETH liquidity is in short supply, in a traditional lending protocol, a lender would be stuck waiting for it to return; with Lido Lend, a lender can now utilize the Fallback Exit mechanism while attempting to withdraw which would allow for eligible borrower debt to be utilized to supplement any shortage in available ETH in order to meet the full withdrawal request. If Fallback Exit is utilized, the outstanding debt of relevant borrowers whose collateral is used for the Fallback Exit is also commensurately reduced. This represents a credible withdrawal path, even in adverse market conditions, into an asset that the lender is already (indirectly) exposed to via the lending market mechanism in a clear and understandable manner.
Which borrowers are impacted by Fallback Exits?
Subject to governance approval of proposed protocol specifications, borrower collateral in the case of a Fallback Exit would be taken from borrowers based on a highest-position-risk ordering: those with positions closest to the LLTV ratio would have their collateral utilized first, while borrowers with highly healthy positions are much less likely to be affected by Fallback Exits.
Full details will be available when the technical specification and market parameters are published in the next 2 weeks.
What’s Next?
Over the coming weeks, Lido Lend will progress through the required governance processes needed for general DAO acceptance of the protocol before mainnet launch. As a part of this, more features, technical specifications and audit reports will be made public.

record.title: NEST: tying the buyback threshold to the approved budget — post 1
record.text:
Hi all,
NEST has been live since 10 August (launch thread) and has not bought a single LDO yet. Its budget counter stood at −$542,451 at the end of September and keeps falling on most days. I spent the last few weeks building a full model of the mechanism to understand whether this can be fixed by tuning parameters. Parameter tuning alone does not solve it. The model points instead to the budget and to how profit is defined as the main levers. Below is what I propose, followed by the reasoning. The full report, model and data are linked at the end.
What I propose
Step 1. Now, through votes, no contract changes
1. Cut the Foundations budget for 2027 materially and, in the same vote, set the NEST threshold equal to the approved budget. I am asking for around $30M, about 30% below the current $43.8M. In the model, buybacks start to grow meaningfully from a cut of about 20% (roughly $35M), and a 30% cut roughly doubles them compared with today. The approved Foundations budget would serve as the operating baseline, not as a claim that it captures every DAO outflow; material off-budget spending, such as the $6.06M Kelp-related costs, would need to be reflected separately.
2. Change the threshold only together with the budget. Any increase in spending, during the year or in the next budget, comes as a separate proposal that explains what the money is for and what it delivers, and the threshold rises with it.
3. Keep the surplus share at 50% until a true-up against actual expenses is in place (item 8 below).
4. Publish budget requests with a breakdown by main line items and an estimate of NEST buybacks at that level of spending, and publish quarterly expense reports faster with the same breakdown.
5. Give NEST its own Easy Track top-up program, separate from the limit used for expense payments.
6. Do not use NEST-bought LDO for contributor payouts. Otherwise distributions eat the buybacks. Whether the tokens are burned or locked is a separate decision for the DAO.
Step 2. In parallel, in development
7. Connect additional DAO income that NEST does not currently capture. Treasury income and Earn appear to add roughly $3.3M a year at the H1 2026 run rate. CSM rebates may add further income, but their accounting treatment relative to reported net staking revenue should be confirmed first. The threshold would also need adjusting for referral payouts, which NEST counts before deduction.
Step 3. Later, if the DAO decides
8. A new allocator with a quarterly true-up against actual expenses. It would keep accruing 50% of the daily surplus, then replace that with the actual quarterly result once the report is out: 75% of a quarterly profit goes to buybacks, and a quarterly loss goes into the deficit in full. This is the point where the share of real profit going to buybacks can rise above 50%.
Why
NEST is not buying because staking revenue is below the $40M reserve. With the current module set, the threshold is covered only when ETH is above roughly $2,668, and every weaker day adds to the deficit. The four days between activation and connecting the revenue source added $147,658 to it, but that is a secondary factor.

record.title: Ethereum for Governments and Institutions: Why neutral infrastructure matters now | Ethereum Foundation Blog
record.text:
Current global shifts clearly signal a critical need for shared, neutral digital public infrastructure outside the control of any single centralized actor. As a public, programmable network designed to operate without reliance on any single party, Ethereum was built to address precisely these needs.
Today, the Ethereum Foundation Global Policy Strategy (GPS) team is publishing "Ethereum for Governments and Institutions", a guide for public sector and institutional leaders facing policy and deployment decisions. The report is a non-technical primer covering how Ethereum works, how it is governed, how it compares with perceived alternatives, and where it is already being deployed. This post introduces the report and answers the core questions that motivated its development: why digital infrastructure needs to be neutral and why Ethereum is suited for the role.

[…]
What this means for governments and institutions
Public discourse often reduces Ethereum to a financial tool. That framing fails to account for Ethereum’s capacity as an open, neutral, programmable infrastructure for any system where multiple parties need to coordinate without a trusted intermediary. That includes trade settlement, asset issuance, identity, registries, attestations, public records, supply chain provenance, and tokenized markets.
Many of these use cases are already visible in practice. For instance, Bhutan and Buenos Aires anchored their decentralized digital identity system on Ethereum, enabling users to own their identity and choose the data they want to share. Ethereum-based rails have also been leveraged for managing land records, combating fraud and ensuring the immutability of public records in India.
For many other governments and institutional stakeholders, there are currently two pressing priorities (1) choosing the neutral infrastructure on which to coordinate with other parties while preserving their own sovereignty; and (2) working out how to govern this category of infrastructure that does not fit cleanly into existing regulatory models. These decisions inform each other. A network that is genuinely neutral, with no controlling party to capture or coerce, supports a unique class of public-sector deployment and calls for a different regulatory approach than one that carries such risks.
Ethereum Basics for Governments and Institutions is our effort to inform these decisions by helping stakeholders understand the Ethereum blockchain and how it differs from other infrastructures, including existing intermediated systems and other blockchains.
It is available now here.

record.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve announces the leadership and objectives of its task forces to advance the conduct of monetary policy
record.text:
July 09, 2026
Federal Reserve announces the leadership and objectives of its task forces to advance the conduct of monetary policy
For release at 3:00 p.m. EDT
Share
The Federal Reserve on Thursday announced the leadership and objectives of its task forces to advance the conduct of monetary policy.
"The Federal Reserve's commitment to price stability and maximum employment is unwavering. As is our resolve to pursue our mandate with rigor," said Chairman Kevin Warsh. "The U.S. economy has changed significantly over the last generation, and never more so than right now. Each task force will carefully consider whether policymakers' means and methods, analytical tools and policy approaches can be improved upon. I am honored that the best minds from a range of disciplines have agreed to work with us to sharpen our performance as an institution. The goal is straightforward: to ensure the Fed is best positioned to achieve our objectives in this consequential time."
The five task forces will examine areas central to the broad conduct of monetary policy. They will be co-led by external advisers—accomplished economists, business leaders, and former central bank practitioners—with deep expertise in their fields. Supported by Federal Reserve staff, they will operate independently, with a mandate to follow the evidence, provide candid feedback, and produce rigorous findings for the Federal Open Market Committee.

[…]
More information on the task forces and topics will be posted periodically on the Federal Reserve's website.

On the Ethereum Foundation's Protocol Security team, we've been running coordinated AI agents against the kinds of systems the network depends on, like systems software, cryptographic code, and contracts that have to be right. The agents found real bugs. One is now public: a remotely-triggerable panic in libp2p's gossipsub, a core part of the peer-to-peer layer Ethereum consensus clients run on, fixed and disclosed as CVE-2026-34219 with credit to the team.
Agents finding bugs wasn't the surprise. The surprise was how little of the work went into finding them, and how much went into telling the real bugs from the ones that just looked real.
This post is for client teams and security researchers who want to do the same thing. It covers how we organize the agents, the bar a candidate has to clear before it counts as a finding, and the habits that keep the results trustworthy.

[…]
A person makes the final call: agents suggest. They don't decide what's real, what's a duplicate of a known issue, or what gets disclosed and when.

June 24, 2026
Federal Reserve Board's annual bank stress test confirms that large banks are well positioned to weather a severe recession and able to continue to lend to households and businesses
For release at 4:00 p.m. EDT
Share
The results of the Federal Reserve Board's annual bank stress test confirmed that large banks are well positioned to weather a severe recession and able to continue to lend to households and businesses. Despite absorbing more than $708 billion in total losses under this year's hypothetical scenario, capital declined only 1.6 percentage points in aggregate, staying above minimum capital requirements.
"Today's results underscore the strength of the banking system," Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman said. "As we work to increase the transparency and accountability of the stress test, public feedback will help us continue to improve and instill greater confidence in the stress test and its results."
As the Board previously announced, today's results will not impact large bank capital requirements, which have been published today. The current capital requirements will stay in place until 2027, when the stress test will be run with loss-estimating models that take public feedback into consideration.
All 32 banks tested remained above their minimum common equity tier 1 capital requirements during this year's hypothetical recession scenario, which was similar in severity to the prior test. The hypothetical scenario this year included a severe global recession with a 39 percent decline in commercial real estate prices and a 30 percent decline in house prices. The unemployment rate also increased to a peak of 10 percent, and economic output declined commensurately.
Three main factors influenced the results of this year's test, with two leading to a larger decline in the aggregate capital ratio than last year, and one more than offsetting this decline:
Projected capital decreased from higher loan losses due to increased loan balances and the increased severity of certain scenario variables;
Projected capital decreased from lower projected unrealized gains in bank securities due to smaller hypothetical declines in interest rates during the scenario; and
Projected capital increased from higher interest income due to recent bank financial performance and smaller hypothetical declines of interest rates during the scenario.
The total projected losses include roughly $200 billion in credit card losses, $160 billion in losses from commercial and industrial loans, and $75 billion in losses from commercial real estate.
For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955.

record.text:
Hi all,
NEST has been live since 10 August (launch thread) and has not bought a single LDO yet. Its budget counter stood at −$542,451 at the end of September and keeps falling on most days. I spent the last few weeks building a full model of the mechanism to understand whether this can be fixed by tuning parameters. Parameter tuning alone does not solve it. The model points instead to the budget and to how profit is defined as the main levers. Below is what I propose, followed by the reasoning. The full report, model and data are linked at the end.
What I propose
Step 1. Now, through votes, no contract changes
1. Cut the Foundations budget for 2027 materially and, in the same vote, set the NEST threshold equal to the approved budget. I am asking for around $30M, about 30% below the current $43.8M. In the model, buybacks start to grow meaningfully from a cut of about 20% (roughly $35M), and a 30% cut roughly doubles them compared with today. The approved Foundations budget would serve as the operating baseline, not as a claim that it captures every DAO outflow; material off-budget spending, such as the $6.06M Kelp-related costs, would need to be reflected separately.
2. Change the threshold only together with the budget. Any increase in spending, during the year or in the next budget, comes as a separate proposal that explains what the money is for and what it delivers, and the threshold rises with it.
3. Keep the surplus share at 50% until a true-up against actual expenses is in place (item 8 below).
4. Publish budget requests with a breakdown by main line items and an estimate of NEST buybacks at that level of spending, and publish quarterly expense reports faster with the same breakdown.
5. Give NEST its own Easy Track top-up program, separate from the limit used for expense payments.
6. Do not use NEST-bought LDO for contributor payouts. Otherwise distributions eat the buybacks. Whether the tokens are burned or locked is a separate decision for the DAO.
Step 2. In parallel, in development
7. Connect additional DAO income that NEST does not currently capture. Treasury income and Earn appear to add roughly $3.3M a year at the H1 2026 run rate. CSM rebates may add further income, but their accounting treatment relative to reported net staking revenue should be confirmed first. The threshold would also need adjusting for referral payouts, which NEST counts before deduction.
Step 3. Later, if the DAO decides
8. A new allocator with a quarterly true-up against actual expenses. It would keep accruing 50% of the daily surplus, then replace that with the actual quarterly result once the report is out: 75% of a quarterly profit goes to buybacks, and a quarterly loss goes into the deficit in full. This is the point where the share of real profit going to buybacks can rise above 50%.
Why
NEST is not buying because staking revenue is below the $40M reserve. With the current module set, the threshold is covered only when ETH is above roughly $2,668, and every weaker day adds to the deficit. The four days between activation and connecting the revenue source added $147,658 to it, but that is a secondary factor.

record.text:
Current global shifts clearly signal a critical need for shared, neutral digital public infrastructure outside the control of any single centralized actor. As a public, programmable network designed to operate without reliance on any single party, Ethereum was built to address precisely these needs.
Today, the Ethereum Foundation Global Policy Strategy (GPS) team is publishing "Ethereum for Governments and Institutions", a guide for public sector and institutional leaders facing policy and deployment decisions. The report is a non-technical primer covering how Ethereum works, how it is governed, how it compares with perceived alternatives, and where it is already being deployed. This post introduces the report and answers the core questions that motivated its development: why digital infrastructure needs to be neutral and why Ethereum is suited for the role.

[…]
What this means for governments and institutions
Public discourse often reduces Ethereum to a financial tool. That framing fails to account for Ethereum’s capacity as an open, neutral, programmable infrastructure for any system where multiple parties need to coordinate without a trusted intermediary. That includes trade settlement, asset issuance, identity, registries, attestations, public records, supply chain provenance, and tokenized markets.
Many of these use cases are already visible in practice. For instance, Bhutan and Buenos Aires anchored their decentralized digital identity system on Ethereum, enabling users to own their identity and choose the data they want to share. Ethereum-based rails have also been leveraged for managing land records, combating fraud and ensuring the immutability of public records in India.
For many other governments and institutional stakeholders, there are currently two pressing priorities (1) choosing the neutral infrastructure on which to coordinate with other parties while preserving their own sovereignty; and (2) working out how to govern this category of infrastructure that does not fit cleanly into existing regulatory models. These decisions inform each other. A network that is genuinely neutral, with no controlling party to capture or coerce, supports a unique class of public-sector deployment and calls for a different regulatory approach than one that carries such risks.
Ethereum Basics for Governments and Institutions is our effort to inform these decisions by helping stakeholders understand the Ethereum blockchain and how it differs from other infrastructures, including existing intermediated systems and other blockchains.
It is available now here.
